place.zh: 黑松岭 · 第二十七道记号
place.en: Black Pine Ridge · the twenty-seventh mark

setup.zh: 第二十七道记号那里，是一段贴着山崖的窄坡。爹的左膝盖罢了工，整个人往崖外一歪——离你两步，坡外是崖。
setup.en: At the twenty-seventh mark the path is a narrow slope hugging the cliff. Father's left knee gives way and he pitches toward the edge — two steps from you, and the cliff beyond.

recap.zh: 暴雨里，你在风歇的空当把爹拽回了山壁，自己却给甩下了崖，摔进谷底的厚苔藓：先查伤，再找路，活到爹来的时候。
recap.en: In the storm you hauled Father back against the rock in the lulls of the wind, and were flung over the edge yourself, into thick moss on the valley floor: check the hurts first, then find a way, and stay alive till Father comes.

zh: 贴着山崖的窄坡，第二十七道记号。
en: A narrow slope on the cliff; the twenty-seventh mark.
The wind comes in gusts, and lulls.

story.zh: 第二十七道记号那里，是一段贴着山崖的窄坡。他爹的左膝盖在这里软了一下。它这一辈子跟他爹聊了无数回天，这一回却一句也没聊，干干脆脆地罢了工，他爹整个人便往崖外一歪。
story.en: At the twenty-seventh mark the path became a narrow slope hugging the cliff. There his father's left knee gave way. All its life it had chatted with his father countless times; this time it said not a word, simply downed tools, and his father pitched toward the edge.

label.en: Check yourself, one thing at a time

exits.means: checks the injuries, gets up carefully, looks for shelter and a way

story.zh:
小满想都没想——不对，他想了，而且想得飞快，快得像他娘拨算盘珠子：离他爹两步，坡外是崖；去拉他，爷儿俩可能一起下去；不拉他，他一定下去。这笔账，不难算。

说时迟那时快，小满扑将过去，一把抓住他爹的腰带，拼了命往里一拽，拽得他爹整个人撞在山壁上，「哎哟」一声；他自己却被那股劲一带，甩了出去。他爹回身伸手来抓，手指擦过了他的手腕，终究没抓住。

小满滚了下去。泥浆、石头、断枝、雨水劈头盖脸而来，天和地在他眼前翻了不知多少个跟头，翻得他连哪边是天都分不清了。他护住了头，后背撞上一样硬东西，疼得眼前一黑，伸手乱抓，竟抓住了一根藤。

那藤绷得笔直，硬生生把他往下掉的势头拽住了，他挂在半空，长长地松了一口气——藤断了。

「你爷爷的——」话一出口，他才想起来，自己的爷爷便是在这黑松岭里没的，忙又补了一句：「……爷爷，不是说你。」说完把那口气收了回来，继续往下掉。

最后一下，他摔进了一片软乎乎的东西里，却是一层苔藓，极厚极软，像一床吸饱了水的大棉被。他整个人陷进去半尺深，好似一只掉进了大馒头里的蚂蚁。

他没有马上起来。他爹说过，摔了先别急着爬起来，一样一样地查。他先动动手指，手指能动；再动动脚趾，脚趾也能动；膝盖破了，手掌磨掉了一层皮，后背火辣辣的，左手腕肿得像个小馒头，骨头却没断。

他这才坐起身来往上看，崖壁高得望不到顶，一直隐进了雨雾里。

他没有喊，只在心里算：爹被自己拽进了山壁里，没掉下来；他膝盖不好，这么大的雨，他下不来，也不该下来；他会等雨停了，顺着记号回村叫人。四十一道记号，是自己刻的，一道都没歪——除了第一道。所以要做的，便是活到那个时候。

十二岁，一个人，在一个从没来过的山谷里，天又快黑了。他爹说过，打猎的人在山里迷了路，头一件事是找个地方躲雨，第二件事是生火，第三件事才是害怕。小满决定，第三件事先欠着。

雨小了些。他扶着崖壁往前走，每走一段，便在崖壁上划一道，好记得回来的路。

这山谷很是古怪。外面的山长的都是松树、柏树、野栗子，这里的树他却一棵也不认得，叶子银白，薄得透光，雨水落上去也不往下淌，滚成一颗一颗圆溜溜的珠子挂在叶尖上。

他没忍住，伸手碰了一颗，只听得「叮」的一声轻响，像一只极小极小的铃铛，那珠子化作一缕白气，没了。

地上的草也不一样，每一步踩下去，草叶都微微发亮，一圈淡淡的光从他脚底下漾开，又慢慢暗了下去，倒像是在一面水上走路。他走得很轻很轻，也不知为什么，总觉得这里的东西都在睡觉，不该吵醒了它们。

便在这时，他看见了光。山谷最深处，一片给雨水砸出来的浅坑里，有一点银光一明一暗，一明一暗，像是有什么东西在很慢很慢地呼吸。
story.en:
Xiaoman didn't think — no, he did, and thought fast, fast as his mother flicking abacus beads: two steps from his father, the cliff beyond; pull him, and they might both go over; don't, and he certainly would. Not a hard sum. Quick as you like, Xiaoman threw himself forward, grabbed his father's belt, and hauled inward with everything he had, slamming his father against the rock face — *oof* — while the force of it flung Xiaoman himself outward.

His father spun and reached for him; his fingers brushed Xiaoman's wrist and, in the end, didn't catch.

Xiaoman tumbled down. Mud, stones, broken branches, rain came at him from every side; heaven and earth turned who knew how many somersaults before his eyes, till he couldn't tell which way was up. He covered his head; his back struck something hard and the pain blacked out his sight; he clawed wildly and — caught a vine.

The vine went taut and wrenched his fall to a stop; he hung in mid-air and let out a long breath of relief — and the vine snapped.

"Your grandpa's —" The words were out before he remembered that his own grandfather had died right here in Black Pine Ridge, and he hastily added: "…Grandpa, not you." That said, he took his breath back and went on falling.

At the last he landed in something soft — a bed of moss, very thick and very soft, like a great quilt that had soaked up all the water it could hold. He sank in half a foot deep, like an ant fallen into a giant steamed bun.

He didn't get up at once. His father had said: after a fall, don't rush to get up; check yourself, one thing at a time. First he moved his fingers: they moved. Then his toes: they moved too. His knees were broken open, the skin of his palms scraped off, his back on fire, his left wrist swollen like a little steamed bun — but no bones broken.

Only then did he sit up and look: the cliff rose so high he couldn't see the top; it vanished into the rain and mist.

He didn't shout. He reckoned instead: he'd hauled his father into the rock face — his father hadn't fallen. His father's knee was bad; in rain like this he couldn't come down, and shouldn't; he'd wait for the rain to stop and follow the marks back to the village for help. Forty-one marks, cut by his own hand, not one of them crooked — except the first. So the thing to do was stay alive till then.

Twelve years old, alone, in a valley he'd never seen, and night about to fall. His father had said: a hunter lost in the mountains first finds shelter from the rain, second makes a fire, and only third gets frightened. Xiaoman decided the third thing could wait.

The rain eased a little. He made his way along the cliff foot, and every stretch he scratched a line on the rock, to know his way back.

It was a strange valley. The mountains outside grew pine, cypress and wild chestnut; here he knew not one tree. Their leaves were silver-white, so thin the light came through, and the rain on them didn't run off but rolled into round beads that hung at the leaf tips.

He couldn't help touching one: a tiny *ding*, like a very, very small bell, and the bead turned into a wisp of white air and was gone.

The grass was different too: each step, the blades glowed faintly, a ring of pale light spreading out from under his foot and slowly dimming, as though he were walking on water. He walked very, very lightly; he couldn't have said why, but he felt everything here was asleep and oughtn't to be woken.

Then he saw the light. At the very bottom of the valley, in a shallow hollow the rain had beaten out, a point of silver light went bright, then dim, bright, then dim — as if something were breathing, very, very slowly.

refuse.zh: 风一阵紧一阵松。等它歇一口气，再拽。
refuse.en: The wind comes in gusts. Wait for it to catch its breath, then pull.
